battle.name: 管崇起義
battle.theater: 陳州、汝南、潁川（河南淮北）
battle.brief: 大業九年（613），隋煬帝第三次征高句麗、漕運告急之際，陳國陳州地界爆發管崇起義，隋廷以郡兵與關中精兵鎮壓，同楊玄感黎陽之變、王薄山東舉事相應，河北、山東、江南的亂勢自此連成一片。卡面亞述長矛並非中土之物，其短柄長刃、配鐵鏃的近身刺擊邏輯，可與隋軍步騎所用的槊、矛同參。

kit.name: 亞述長矛
kit.history: 短柄、長刃，配著鐵鏃。亞述人把它和弓、鐵器綁在一起，兩河流域的城一個接一個陷落。

countries: 這場起義的交戰雙方，一方是隋朝中央政府，一方是陳國一帶的民間武裝。隋朝此時是全中國最有效率的國家機器：中央有十二衛與各軍府，地方有州郡兵與縣兵，軍令由行臺尚書令、郡守層層下達，運河北段的漕船把江南的米運到洛口倉再轉輸前線。代價是抽空河南的壯丁與糧食去做第三次征高句麗，中原只剩郡兵與臨時募來的鄉勇可用。起義方是陳國（治所在今河南淮陽一帶）的鄉里武裝，首領管崇，兵眾來源是本地失去土地與役期的農民、逃戶與散卒，既沒有常備建制，也沒有後勤與指揮系統，僅靠一州一縣的地理熟悉度與同鄉關係維繫。值得注意的是，這不是一場孤立的叛亂：大業九年二月，禮部尚書楊玄感在黎陽起兵，兵眾十餘萬，直逼洛陽；山東長平的王薄以「知世郎」為號，寫出「無向遼東浪死歌」散傳單號召；河北清河、渤海一帶有張金象、孫安祖、高舉等聚眾為亂。管崇的起義正是在這一整片同時冒頭的局面裡發生，各股勢力彼此聲援而互不從屬，隋廷必須分兵應付。壓制方的主力是山東、河北戰線上的名將張須陀，他以騎兵馳援各處，配合郡兵守城屯田，到次年才把主要的幾股起義壓下去。
countriesEn: The two sides in this rising were, on one side, the central government of the Sui and, on the other, a local armed band from the state of Chen. The Sui at that moment was the most efficient state machine in all of China: the centre had the twelve imperial guards and the various army headquarters, the localities had prefectural, commandery and county troops, orders ran down through the provincial administration and the commandery governors, and the grain barges of the northern Grand Canal carried rice from the south to the Luokou granary at Luoyang and thence to the front. The price was the emptying of the central plain of able-bodied men and grain for the third campaign against Goguryeo, leaving only commandery troops and hastily recruited local braves to hold the interior. The insurgents were a village levy from the state of Chen, whose seat lay in what is now southern Henan around Huaiyang, led by Guan Chong and drawn from landless peasants, absentees from the registers and demobilised men of the region; they had no standing establishment, no logistics and no command structure, and existed only through their familiarity with one prefecture at a time and through ties of neighbourhood. It is important to note that this was not an isolated revolt. In the second month of the ninth year of Daye, the Minister of Rites Yang Xuangan rose at Liyang with more than a hundred thousand men and drove straight at Luoyang; in Changping in Shandong a man named Wang Bo took the title Know-the-World Man and circulated a handbill with the song Never March to Liaodong to Die; and in Qinghe and Bohai in Hebei, Zhang Jinxiang, Sun Anzu and Gao Ju raised bands of their own. Guan Chong's rising broke out in the midst of this whole simultaneity, the various bands supporting one another without obeying one another, and the court had to split its forces to answer each. The weight of the suppression fell on Zhang Xutuo, the famous commander on the Shandong and Hebei front, who brought cavalry to the relief of each threatened point and worked with the prefectural troops holding cities and cultivating the fields; it took him into the following year to crush the main clusters of the rising.
people: 直接留下姓名的只有管崇一人。他是陳國人，史書沒有為他立傳，只在記大業九年諸州郡事跡的編年中留下他起兵、被討平的數語記載，他的年齡、出身、出身部族與下落皆不可考。真正推動全局的是坐在洛陽的隋煬帝楊廣：大業九年正月他調集一百一十三萬大軍第三次東征高句麗，兵分四道自涿郡、萊州、登州、營州出發，京畿與中原的守備因此降到只剩郡兵；同年二月楊玄感在黎陽起兵，十餘萬眾直趨洛陽，煬帝得報後自長城馳返，於虎牢關一帶布防，才把楊玄感逼回黎陽、擊潰於漳水之側，楊玄感與其弟楊諫、楊積善皆死於亂軍。三月之後，中原的起事已呈星散之勢：山東長平有王薄起兵，河北有張金象、孫安祖、高舉等人，陳國有管崇，吳郡一帶另有朱變、沈生等人聚眾，煬帝疲於奔命，只好下詔郡國嚴加捕治。鎮壓方真正可以依靠的名字是弘農華陰人張須陀，他在大業九年至十一年間以精騎往來山東、河北，屢破張金象、王薄、劉什子等部，每戰輒斬獲甚眾，隋廷倚之為平叛的柱石；然張須陀卒於大業十一年，其後平叛便再無統一名將主持，隋廷只能靠分派各路將領各自剿辦，遂陷於疲於奔命而收功甚微的窘境。
peopleEn: Only one name is directly recorded: that of Guan Chong himself. He was a man of the state of Chen, and no biography was ever written for him; he survives only in a few lines within the annalistic record of the affairs of the prefectures in the ninth year of Daye, and his age, his family, his tribal or local affiliation and his fate are all beyond recovery. The man who really shaped the situation sat in Luoyang: Yang Guang, the Sui Yangdi. In the first month of the ninth year of Daye he mustered 1,130,000 men for a third expedition against Goguryeo, splitting them into four columns moving out from Zhuojun, Laizhou, Dengzhou and elsewhere, so that the garrison of the capital region and of the central plain was reduced to the commandery troops. In the second month Yang Xuangan rose at Liyang with more than a hundred thousand men and drove at Luoyang, and the emperor rode back from the Great Wall to take up a defensive line around Hulao Pass, where he forced Yang Xuangan back to Liyang and destroyed him by the side of the Zhang River; Yang Xuangan and his brothers Yang Jian and Yang Jishan were all killed in the rout. From the third month onward the risings in the plain came to resemble scattered sparks: Wang Bo in Changping in Shandong, Zhang Jinxiang, Sun Anzu and Gao Ju in Hebei, Guan Chong in the state of Chen, and in the Wu prefecture further south men named Zhu Bian and Shen Sheng. The emperor was exhausted by all this and issued orders to the prefectures to search and seize with severity. The name the suppression could really rely on was that of Zhang Xutuo of Huayin in Hongnong, who rode between Shandong and Hebei in the ninth, tenth and eleventh years of Daye, breaking Zhang Jinxiang, Wang Bo and Liu Shizi again and again and taking heavy captures in every action, and whom the court treated as the pillar of the pacification. But Zhang Xutuo died in the eleventh year of Daye, and after his death there was no single commander left to direct the suppression; the court could only detach different generals to different districts to hunt down the bands, and so found itself running endlessly without securing much.
kits: 卡面上的亞述長矛並不曾出現在陳國的戰場上：它是兩河流域的兵器，約公元前九百年前後亞述人用短柄長刃配鐵鏃的刺擊兵器，與弓、斧、鐵器配合使用，靠成排步兵在近身格鬥中撕開缺口，配合攻城塔與撞車使兩河流域的城邑逐一陷落。放到隋末中原的裝備譜系裡，它對應的是同一條技術路線上更晚、更長的兵器——隋軍的槊。隋代步騎通用的主兵器是槊，長桿、單刃、有鋒，騎兵持槊衝鋒、步兵結陣以槊抵禦，與亞述短柄長刃長矛同屬「以刺擊換取正面突破」的邏輯，但尺度大得多、桿長足以讓後排的戰士在第一排倒下後接替上來。刀兵器方面，隋已完成從環首刀向直刃刀過渡，橫刀、直刀與佩刀並用，環首刀僅殘存於儀仗與裝備雜抄中；弓弩仍是遠程主力，角胎桑木弓配合大臂弩、蹶張弩，攻城時另有石砲、雲梯、撞車、飛橋、鉤援一類器械，據《隋書》記隋軍曾造攻城之器與「萬石弩」一類的重型弩機。防護為明光鎧與漆木盾，騎兵多不具全裝甲，只有少數精騎披具裝馬鎧。起義一方則完全不是這個世界：農具改造成兵器，鋤、斧、叉、環刀與削尖的竹木梃並行，礪石掛在腰間，鎧甲極少，攻城無雲梯、撞車可恃，只能靠夜襲、守土、斷糧與鄉民熟悉街巷之便行事；這一支軍隊的戰鬥力來自腳程與熟悉度，而不是裝備。
kitsEn: The Assyrian spear on the card never appeared on a battlefield in the state of Chen: it belongs to the military repertoire of the two river lands, a thrusting weapon of short haft, long blade and iron point used by the Assyrians from around 900 BC, wielded together with the bow, the axe and other iron gear, so that ranks of infantry could tear gaps in close combat and, working with siege towers and battering rams, brought the cities of Mesopotamia down one after another. Placed in the equipment spectrum of the late Sui central plain, it corresponds to the same technical line in a later and much longer form, the shao of the Sui army. The principal weapon of Sui foot and horse was the shao: a long shaft, single edged, with a point, carried by cavalry in the charge and by infantry in the line to meet the enemy, following the same logic of winning a breakthrough by thrusting that the short-hafted Assyrian spear followed, but on a far greater scale, its shaft long enough that the men of the second rank could step forward when the first fell. Among blade weapons the Sui had completed the transition from ring-pommel swords to straight-edged ones, using the heng dao, the zhi dao and the pei dao, while the ring-pommel dao survived only in ceremonial display and in miscellaneous equipment lists. Bows and crossbows remained the main missile arm, with horn-and-mulberry bows backed by heavy arm bows and the蹶張 crossbow, and for siege work there were stone throwers, scaling ladders, battering rams, flying bridges and grappling irons; the Sui Shu records that the army built siege engines and heavy crossbows of the ten-thousand-dan class. Protection was the bright armour and the lacquered wooden shield; the cavalry were not generally fully armoured, only a few picked units wearing horse and rider armour together. The insurgents lived in an entirely different world: farm tools turned into weapons, with hoes, axes, pitchforks, ring-pommelled sabres and sharpened bamboo or wooden clubs all in use, whetstones hung at the waist, armour very scarce and no scaling ladder or battering ram to rely on, so that they could only work by night attack, by holding ground, by cutting supplies, and by knowing the lanes and byways of their own villages. The fighting power of that force came from marching and from local familiarity, not from equipment.
tactics: 起義軍的戰術完全受制於兵力與器械：正面強攻州郡城牆是不可能的，因為沒有撞車、雲梯與足夠的投石器具，所以他們選擇的是「不攻城、困城、亂城」的路子——夜間由鄉民引路突入城郊的倉場與官署，奪取糧食與兵器，解除維持治安的縣吏與巡兵的職守與武裝，逼迫官府放棄次要城堡，把力量集中到郡城周圍；同時以小股騎兵或步卒襲擊糧道、截斷漕船與徵發車隊，令遠在江都、洛陽的朝廷無法把兵糧送到前線。隋廷的反制則是多線並行的：張須陀以精騎作戰，取其疾速與衝擊力，專打散兵與不據城者；郡兵則依城固守、據屯田與鄉里徵發就地補充兵員，避免被拉出城郊；中央另以政令配合，安撫受脅迫的鄉里，許以赦免與復歸，試圖把「附亂者」與「首謀者」分開。前線最大的弱點是距離：洛陽到陳州近五百里，淮北一線的郡兵一旦被牽制，補充多靠騎兵晝夜兼程，糧秣則取自洛口倉與沿汴、泗、淮的轉運，一旦運河上游被擾，遠征軍與平叛軍便同時缺糧。整場戰事因此呈現反覆拉鋸的形態：起義方以「散」為生存，官方以「快」為取勝之術，雙方都在比拼誰更能承受消耗。
tacticsEn: The tactics of the insurgents were entirely determined by their numbers and their equipment. A frontal assault on the walls of a commandery or prefecture city was out of the question, for they had no battering ram, no scaling ladder and no adequate stone throwers, so their line was the one of not storming the city but strangling it and throwing it into disorder: by night, guided by villagers, they struck the granaries and the official compounds outside the walls, took food and weapons, disarmed the county clerks and the patrol soldiers who kept order, and forced the authorities to abandon their lesser castles, concentrating their strength in the neighbourhood of the commandery seat. At the same time they sent small bodies of horse and foot against the supply line, cutting the grain barges and the levy convoys so that the court at Jiangdu and Luoyang could not get men and grain forward. The court's counter-measure ran on several lines at once. Zhang Xutuo fought with picked cavalry, taking his speed and shock against bands that dispersed and did not hold towns; the commandery troops stayed behind their walls, worked the fields and drew replacements locally from their own districts so as not to be drawn out into the open; and in the centre the government worked with proclamations, reassuring the coerced villagers, promising pardon and restoration, and trying to separate the men who had been swept along from the men who had planned the rising. The greatest weakness of the front was distance. Luoyang is close to five hundred li from Chenzhou, so once the commandery troops of the Huai northern line were pinned, reinforcement had to come by cavalry riding day and night, while grain came from the Luokou granary and from the transfer of supplies along the Bian, the Si and the Huai. Whenever the upper reaches of the canal were disturbed, the expeditionary army and the army of suppression went hungry at the same time. The whole war therefore took the form of repeated seesaw: the insurgents survived by scattering, the court won by moving fast, and each side was in effect trying to see who could bear the strain of exhaustion the longer.
data: 可核對的數字分為軍國總量與本場局部兩類。軍國總量方面：開皇三年定制州九十三、縣四百一十四；開皇五年頒行戶等與新律，開皇九年大索貌閱，得天下四百六十餘萬戶、二千三百餘萬丁口，這是隋朝鼎盛時的戶口基準；開皇十年罷諸州都督府兵，兵歸農，州郡改募兵，府兵制解體；大業三年改州為郡，置郡一百九十餘。大業九年正月征高句麗，兵額一百一十三萬，分四道進攻，一度深入至平壤、扶餘，卻因糧盡與酷暑而大敗，士卒死亡十之七八，返者不及原數三分之一，這是隋廷當年最大的一筆人力耗費。局部方面：楊玄感黎陽起兵眾十餘萬，為同年規模最大者；王薄起兵眾數萬，散傳單行於齊郡；河北張金象、孫安祖、高舉、劉什子各聚眾數萬至數萬不等；管崇一軍的確切人數史無明文，只能從同年淮北各部相繼響應、隋廷必須分兵四處的記載推測其為數千至數萬之眾，未能確證。戰役時間亦無確日，只知起於大業九年、至十年之間被平。
dataEn: The verifiable figures fall into two kinds, those of the state as a whole and those of this particular rising. For the state: in the third year of Kaihuang there were established ninety-three departments and four hundred and fourteen counties; in the fifth year of Kaihuang the household registers and the new code were promulgated, and in the ninth year of Kaihuang the great enumeration of the population produced a count of rather more than 4,600,000 households and some 23,000,000 persons, the benchmark of the Sui at its height; in the tenth year of Kaihuang the commandery army headquarters were abolished, the soldiers were returned to the fields, and the prefectures switched to recruited troops, which dissolved the fubing system; in the third year of Daye the departments were reorganised as commanderies, some one hundred and ninety of them. In the first month of the ninth year of Daye the expedition against Goguryeo was raised to 1,130,000 men, moving out in four columns, reaching as far as Pyongyang and Buyeo, and was then badly defeated for want of grain and in the terrible heat, with seven or eight men in ten of the troops dying and fewer than a third of the number mustered making it back: this was the single largest drain on the manpower of the realm that year. For the rising itself: Yang Xuangan's army at Liyang numbered more than a hundred thousand, the largest of that year; Wang Bo drew a few thousand men and distributed his handbill through the Qi commandery; in Hebei, Zhang Jinxiang, Sun Anzu, Gao Ju and Liu Shizi raised bands of from several thousand to tens of thousands each. For Guan Chong's own force the records give no exact figure at all, and it can only be inferred, from the fact that the court had to divide its troops in four directions along the northern Huai, that it amounted to some thousands or tens of thousands; the point cannot be proved. The dates of the rising are equally imprecise: only that it began in the ninth year of Daye and was pacified by the time of the tenth.
cause: 起義的成因分遠近兩層。遠層是隋朝制度的崩損：文帝末年已罷府兵、府兵歸農而改募兵，兵不再與農田相繫，國家失去可以快速召集的常備武力；同時均田與戶等制在江南豪族兼併與官吏庇蔭下已名存實亡，無力再按丁口徵發；加之文帝晚期連年興役、巡遊，役使與和市之制在民間早已怨聲載道。近層是導火線：大業九年正月一百一十三萬大軍第三次東征，河北、山東、江南的丁壯與牛馬被抽調一空，運河漕船盡數北上，糧價騰貴而漕運斷續，淮北各州縣既要供應前線，又自給不足，一旦有一處出亂子，郡兵既無馬可騎、亦無糧可食。楊玄感之變所以能牽動全局，也在於他給了天下人一個榜樣：黎陽的起兵並非烏合之眾，而是尚書令級別的官員在起義，隋廷的處置卻暴露出中樞對河南的調度遲緩。管崇起義正是這種榜樣效應在淮北的一次回響，加上陳國一帶州郡密集、漕運與徵發同時壓在鄉里頭上，官府與民間的衝突比其他地方更直接。此外，煬帝即位後猜忌宗室、誅除異己，楊勇一系的舊人與河南行臺的官僚心中不平，這層政治怨恨也讓陳國的鄉里更容易被號召。
causeEn: The causes of the rising work at two levels. At the deeper level lies the disintegration of the Sui institutions. Already in the last years of Wendi the fubing had been abolished, the soldiery returned to the fields and recruitment took its place, so that the state lost the standing force it could summon quickly; at the same time the equal-field system and the household registers had become nominal in the face of the consolidation of great families in the south and the protection of officials, and could no longer draw service on a per-capita basis; and the campaigns and tours of the late Wendi had already left the empire with a standing grievance over corvée and the compulsory purchase of goods. At the nearer level lies the trigger. In the first month of the ninth year of Daye 1,130,000 men were mustered for the third eastern expedition: the able-bodied men, the draught animals and the grain boats of Hebei, Shandong and the south were all drawn away, grain prices rose steeply and the canal traffic broke off, so that the prefectures of the northern Huai had to provision the front while provisioning themselves poorly, and once trouble broke out in one place the commandery troops had neither horses to ride nor grain to eat. Yang Xuangan's rising shook the whole empire because it offered the country a model: the rising at Liyang was not a mob but an official of ministerial rank in arms, and the court's handling of it exposed how slowly the centre could shift troops within Henan. Guan Chong's rising was an echo of that model in the northern Huai, aggravated by the concentration of prefectures and commanderies there, where canal service and levy pressing fell on the same villages at once, so that the friction between the officials and the people was far more direct than elsewhere. In addition, the emperor's mistrust of his own kin and his purge of dissent after accession, and the resentment of the old men of Yang Yong's faction and of the officials of the Henan provincial administration, made the villages of Chen easier to call.
impact: 這一場起義本身的直接戰果極小：它在大業九年內即被平定，未能佔據一座大城，也沒有匯入瓦崗或河北的巨流。但它的意義在於顯示隋朝的統治已從中心向外逐層剝落——陳國一鄉的武力都能在數月之內攻破州縣的治安、斷掉一段糧道，則更東、更北的地方自然更容易跟進。管崇之亂與同年其他起義一道，把中原的州縣秩序從「郡兵足以守土」推回到「必須靠中央的騎兵 才能彈壓」的地步，而每一次彈壓都要消耗數千名兵卒的性命與數十日的漕運。從更長的視角看，淮北的起義為大業十三年以後的更大崩潰預先鬆動了地方基層：陳留、杞、雍丘一帶的流民與池兵，日後正是李密瓦崗軍的兵源與地盤；而隋廷在淮北的失血，也讓它無法同時應付北邊的突厥與南邊的江南。江南方面，朱變、沈生等在吳郡起兵、劫掠州縣，與淮北的亂事同一年爆發，隋朝由此明白南北皆不可恃。等到大業十四年江都之圍與大業十七年的江都弒逆，隋亡已無可挽回。
impactEn: The direct military results of this rising were very small: it was put down within the year, it never held a great city, and it never fed into the great movements of Wagang or of the northern plain. Its significance lies instead in showing that Sui control was peeling away from the centre outward. If the armed men of a single district of Chen could break the policing of the prefectures, cut a stretch of the supply road and hold the field for months, then everything further east and further north would plainly be easier to join. Guan Chong's rising, together with the others of the same year, pushed the order of the central plain back from the point where a commandery garrison sufficed to hold its ground to the point where only cavalry dispatched from the centre could repress it, and each repression cost thousands of soldiers' lives and a month of canal traffic. In the longer view, the rising in the northern Huai loosened the local base for the far greater collapse that came after the thirteenth year of Daye. The refugees and the disbanded soldiers around Chenliu, Qi and Yongqiu were to become exactly the manpower and the ground of Li Mi's Wagang army; and the bleeding that the Sui suffered in the northern Huai left it unable to deal at the same time with the Turks in the north and the south. In the south, men named Zhu Bian and Shen Sheng rose in the Wu prefecture and raided the prefectures and counties, breaking out in the same year as the troubles in the northern Huai, and the Sui learned that it could rely on neither half of the empire. By the siege of Jiangdu in the fourteenth year of Daye and the murder of the emperor there in the seventeenth, the fate of the dynasty was beyond repair.
result: 結局是短促而明確的：管崇的部眾在隋朝郡兵與中央派出的精騎配合下被掃平，陳國一帶的州縣秩序在數月之後復歸朝廷控制，隋廷的處置也從此更趨嚴酷——郡國捕亡的詔令接連而下，首謀者斬，首惡者送京師族誅，受脅從者許其自新，地方上的武裝團體被逐一解散。管崇本人及其部眾的下落，在存世的編年記載中並無交代，其名此後再未出現於正史；這是隋末大量起義者的共同命運，多數首領在史冊上只留下「起兵—被討平」兩個節點。從戰役層面看，管崇起義既沒有改變陳國的行政建置，也沒有動搖隋朝在淮北的統治形式，隋煬帝仍以河南行臺節制淮北諸郡，郡兵制度、戶等徵發與漕運轉輸一仍其舊。真正被改變的是力量的對比：此後每有郡兵不足、運河受阻之地，叛亂的號召就多一分成算，隋朝的地方官員也開始明白，靠郡兵與一紙詔令已不足以彈壓鄉里之亂。這一課在十八年的大業中沒有被學到，直到李密、竇建德、劉武周相繼起兵、中原大部淪為戰場，隋廷才在兵與糧的雙重枯竭中崩潰。
resultEn: The ending was abrupt and unambiguous: Guan Chong's bands were swept away by the combination of the Sui commandery troops and the picked cavalry dispatched from the centre, and the administrative order of the prefectures around the state of Chen returned to court control within a few months. The court's handling of it then grew markedly harsher. Edicts ordering the search for runaways were issued one after another: ringleaders were beheaded, the principal offenders were sent to the capital for execution with their clans, those who had been coerced were allowed to come forward and be restored, and the armed bands in the districts were dispersed one by one. The fate of Guan Chong himself and of his followers is not recorded in the surviving annals, and his name never appears again in the official histories; that is the common fate of the leaders of the late Sui risings, most of whom survive in the books as two points only, rising and being put down. At the level of the campaign, nothing was changed: the administrative structure of the state of Chen was untouched, Sui rule in the northern Huai kept its institutional form, Yang Guang continued to hold the northern Huai through the Henan provincial administration, and the commandery troops, the household levies and the transfer of supplies along the canal all went on as before. What did change was the balance of forces. From then on, wherever the garrison was thin or the canal was obstructed, an appeal to revolt carried so much the more weight, and the local officials of the Sui began to understand that commandery troops and a single edict were no longer enough to repress disorder in the villages. That lesson was never learned during the eighteen years of Daye, and the dynasty collapsed only when Li Mi, Dou Jiande and Liu Wuzhou rose in turn and most of the central plain became a battlefield, exhausted of both soldiers and grain.
